derivation: Generated by tools/import_kicad_board.py from the vendor's own KiCad footprint. Pad centres are exact to three decimal places in millimetres, scaled at 8.0 px/mm from a 24.54 x 20.75 mm extent including a 1.0 mm margin. Pin names joined from the symbol library on pad number. Nothing here was measured off an image.
assumption: Every `pin` is null: that field is the rcontrol pin index of a PICSimLab board implementation (webui/pinmap.py), and none exists for this board. `chip_pin` and `chip_index` are what tools/import_pindefs.py read out of the sources named in `pindefs`: the vendor's own CAD, `seeed-pcb`, for `NFC2`, `NFC1`, and the board-support packages for the rest; a pad whose `chip_pin` is null says why in `why_null`. No board module describes nRF54LM20A here, so no level is read for any pad and the pin view reports every one as not modelled until a module and a core exist; `chip_pin` is recorded so that the join is ready, not made. 10 pins on this board are named with NO flat number -- P1.02, P3.04, P3.05, and so on -- so every pad reaching one carries `chip_index` null for that reason and not for a missing reading: no flat GPIO numbering is published for the nRF54LM20A at all, so a module for it would key its own table the way webui/boards/samd21.py does, and until one exists no level is read for any pad here.

pindefs.derivation: Generated by tools/import_pindefs.py from the sources in `packages`, at those revisions, and not every one of them is a board-support package. The vendor's own CAD among them, `seeed-pcb`, answered `NFC2`, `NFC1`; the board-support packages, `zephyr`, answered every other pad that resolves. Nothing was inferred from the silkscreen or a pinout image: a label resolves only when every source in `packages` that defines it names the same pin, and `python tools/import_pindefs.py <board>` prints the file that named it.
